paper_metadata.title: A 0-dB IL 2140 30 MHz Bandpass Filter Utilizing Q-Enhanced Spiral Inductors in Standard CMOS
paper_metadata.abstract: A 3-pole Chebyshev bandpass filter, that employs on-chip passive elements with -enhancement technique, achieves an insertion loss of 0 dB and a passband of 60 MHz around a center frequency of 2140 MHz. The -enhancement technique is based on coupled-inductor negative resistance generator. In contrast to conventional negative resistance generator, this technique compensates resonator loss without introducing distortion in the filter response in the passband. Fabricated in a 0.25m CMOS, the filter consumes 7 mA from a 2.5-V supply. The filter occupies an area of 1.3 mm 2.7 mm. Terms—Bandpass filters, CMOS analog integrated Index circuits, coupled inductor, negative resistance, enhancement, resonator, spiral inductor, W-CDMA.

Two common bandpass filter topologies are ladder and narrowband-coupled-resonator topologies (Fig. 9).
The ladder topology [Fig. 9(a)] utilizes both series and parallel resonators.
The first type is called top-C-coupled topology [Fig. 9(b)] where a capacitor is used to couple parallel resonators together.
Inductors can also be used to couple resonators together, resulting in top-L coupled topology [Fig. 9(c)].

Furthermore, this topology maximizes, rather than minimizes, the number of inductors that -enhanced. need to be A more suitable topology is a shunt-C-coupled topology [Figs. 9(d) and 10] where only series resonators are used and shunt capacitors are reasonably sized for on-chip realization.
